title: Composing Application: Harmony, Texture & Song Forms
welcome_lead: Layer your ideas: combine melody with chords, choose textures, and shape pop songs and rondos.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Start with the primary chords I, IV and V. In C major these are C, F and G. Try matching each strong beat of your melody to a chord — usually the melody note belongs to that chord.

Change chord every 1 or 2 bars to keep momentum without sounding restless.

Homophonic texture (melody + chords) is the everyday texture of pop and hymns. Polyphonic texture has two or more independent melodies — great for variety.

Vary your texture across sections: start thin, build to a thick chorus, drop back to a sparse bridge.

A pop song typically follows intro – verse – chorus – verse – chorus – bridge – chorus. The chorus is the catchiest part and usually repeats with the same words.

Rondo form (ABACA) returns to a familiar refrain between contrasting episodes — popular in Classical-era finales.
